Cerrion launches video-based process monitoring solution
Abies deployed Cerrion AI Agents on its bottleneck timber transfer conveyors and extended automation across the entire production.

By deploying Cerrion AI Agents on its key timber transfer conveyors, Abies enabled an autonomous, closed-loop response to transport anomalies. This significantly accelerated resolution times and reduced downtime by 70% on those assets - while building the confidence to extend automation across the entire production area and set the foundation for unmanned production.

Abies’ wood-processing lines operate at high speeds, where even small deviations in material flow can escalate quickly. Boards may skew, accumulate, jam, or break at transfer points. If not addressed immediately, these issues can block production, require manual intervention, reduce throughput, and put unnecessary strain on surrounding equipment.

One recurring problem area was the trim-and-measure cross-transfer conveyors - especially at the transfer end. When timber jammed in this zone, it had to be detected instantly to prevent longer stoppages.
Continuously monitor critical production areas

At Abies, Cerrion AI Agents were deployed on 10 existing cameras covering the bottleneck infeed trim-and-measure cross-transfer conveyors but also other key transfer and wood processing areas, such as planers, elevating conveyors and board splitters.

Each event is also recorded in Cerrion’s shop floor applications, creating a clear basis for follow-up. This helps operators and line leaders understand what happened and continuously improve the process in a more structured way over time.
Autonomous preventive line stops before blockages occur
Clear path to run additional production areas unmanned with Cerrion AI Agents
From downtime reduction to autonomous production
After achieving a 70% reduction in downtime on the infeed trim-and-measure cross-transfer conveyors, Abies expanded the deployment from 10 to 22 cameras across the entire production.

With Cerrion’s AI Agents now live throughout the factory, Abies is using the technology as a foundation for more autonomous production. The results from the initial deployment demonstrated that Cerrion AI Agents can go beyond monitoring and enable real-time operational control.

Building on this success, Abies plans to make one key production area run fully autonomously with Cerrion. The goal is not only to detect deviations, but also to trigger the right response instantly, creating a more stable production flow with less reliance on operators.
